record.question: Which one of the following statements does not describe geography?
options: Its core concepts are space, place and time
record.explanation: The PDF (Sept 2017, Technical Paper II, p.1) lists the options as printed. Geography is commonly described as integrative, subject to dualism, and concerned with man-environment relations, but its core concepts are usually given as space, place, region, scale and related terms rather than time, so the statement that does not describe geography is the one about space, place and time.

record.question: The rank-size rule does not work when one considers the distribution of
options: All of the citizens in a given country
All of the cities in a given country
All of the counties, provinces, or parishes within a given state
All of the polities within a given region
record.explanation: Printed page 6 confirms "citizens", rather than cities. The rank-size rule relates the populations of settlements or territorial units to their ranks (approximately P_r = P_1/r); individual citizens do not constitute differently sized population units. record.question: Whittlesey has taken all the following criteria to classify agricultural regions EXCEPT
options: The method used to grow the crops and produce the stocks
The intensity of application to the land of labour, capital and organization, and the outturn of the product which results.
The disposal of the products for marketing
record.explanation: Printed page 8 confirms "for marketing". Whittlesey's original fourth criterion is disposal for consumption, covering both subsistence on the farm and sale; the first three supplied options reproduce his other criteria, so the restricted marketing wording is the likely intended exception. This is an imperfect distinction because marketing is itself part of product disposal, making the item potentially defective (Whittlesey, 1936, p. 209: https://cbpbu.ac.in/userfiles/file/2020/STUDY_MAT/GEO/Major%20Agricultural%20Regions%20of%20the%20Earth.pdf).

record.question: Electoral geographers study how people in an area are likely to vote, which can be most conclusively linked to the
options: election monitors that visit the area
ballots that the people use in the area
ethnicity of populations outside the area
record.explanation: The physical landscape is the most defensible of the printed choices: classical electoral geography links terrain and agrarian landscapes to settlement, landownership and social structure, which can influence voting. However, "most conclusively" overstates an indirect and context-dependent relationship; landscape alone is not a reliable general predictor, so this proposal remains uncertain (Geography of Elections, discussion of Siegfried: https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9781317601876_A23892994/preview-9781317601876_A23892994.pdf).
